topicName: Ansible Roles: Structure, Dependencies, and Defaults
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Ansible Roles: Structure, Dependencies, and Defaults"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Ansible roles provide a framework for fully independent, reusable collections of variables, tasks, templates, and handlers. By organizing your automation content into standardized role structures, you can easily share code between playbooks, improve maintainability, and scale your infrastructure automation."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Standard Role Directory Structure"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A standard Ansible role follows a specific directory tree. Each directory contains specific types of YAML files and assets. You can use the ansible-galaxy command to automatically generate this scaffolding."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"ansible-galaxy init webserver"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"This command creates the following directory layout:"},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"defaults/: Contains default variables for the role which have the lowest priority and can be easily overridden."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"vars/: Contains higher priority variables specific to the role."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"tasks/: Contains the main list of tasks executed by the role."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"handlers/: Contains handlers, which may be invoked by tasks and can flush notifications."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"templates/: Holds Jinja2 templates that can be deployed to managed nodes."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"files/: Contains static files that need to be transferred to managed nodes."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"meta/: Contains metadata about the role, including author, license, and role dependencies."},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Managing Defaults and Variables"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Role defaults are defined in 'defaults/main.yml'. These variables have the lowest precedence, making them ideal for setting configurable options that users of your role might want to override in their playbooks or group_vars."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"---
# defaults/main.yml
nginx_port: 80
nginx_worker_processes: 'auto'
"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Conversely, variables defined in 'vars/main.yml' have a much higher precedence and should be used for internal role logic that should not be overridden by the end-user."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Configuring Role Dependencies"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Role dependencies allow you to automatically pull in other roles when a specific role is executed. These are defined inside the 'meta/main.yml' file of the parent role. Dependencies are always executed before the main role runs."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"---
# meta/main.yml
dependencies:
  - role: common
  - role: database
    vars:
      db_name: production
"},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Using Roles in a Playbook"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once your role structure, defaults, and dependencies are established, you can invoke the role within a playbook using the 'roles' keyword."},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"---
- hosts: webservers
  become: true
  roles:
    - role: webserver
      nginx_port: 443
"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"By following this modular approach, your Ansible infrastructure automation remains clean, scalable, and easy to test across multiple environments."}]
